author: Rex Smith
title: Woman staying at Wooster Township motel describes escaping fatal fire - NewsBreak
text:
By Rex Smith ,
7 hours ago
WOOSTER TOWNSHIP , Ohio (WJW) — Three people lost their lives during a motel fire in Wooster Township early Wednesday.
The massive destruction of the middle of three buildings at the Econo Lodge was the talk of the town; everyone very sad to learn that a family in one of the rooms did not make it out.
3 dead after fire tears through Wooster Township motel The fire sparked around 1:30 a.m., causing major damage to the structure. Wayne County sheriff’s deputies were the first to arrive on scene. Sheriff Tom Ballinger said they immediately encountered extremely fierce flames going through the roof of the building along with heavy smoke.
But they jumped quickly into action.
“I mean, that was the first thing our deputies did,” he said. “Just started clearing rooms in the area, and like I said, the heat and the smoke were pretty extensive.”
Just moments behind them was Wooster Township firefighters, working to clear all the rooms. Sadly, a family – a man, Hiteshkumar Suthar, and two women, Hinaben Suthar and Isha Suthar – did not survive.
“This is a tragic loss for the family members of these three victims, and we’re trying to do everything we can to find a cause to figure out what happened,” said Wooster Township Fire Chief Dallas Terrell.
Terrell said his department, the sheriff’s office, the state fire marshal’s office and the ATF are all investigating.
The devastation was extremely difficult to witness for those staying at the motel.
Kiera Curry said she heard pounding at her door, someone screaming that there was a fire.
She left her room, faced with extreme heat and smoke to find chaos, people running and screaming. She abandoned most of her things in her room and got to safety.
14-year-old killed in UTV crash in Tuscarawas County She said she’s been staying at a nearby hotel, but can’t get her things from the Econo Lodge. Hours after the fire, she was still in shock.
“My heart goes out to the people that perished in the fire. I don’t really know what to feel for me. Maybe a little bit of survivor’s guilt because I was right there,” she said.
One firefighter was treated and released for burns. The American Red Cross is helping those who were displaced.
